description:
Get information about a specific weakness (CWE), its related attack patterns (CAPEC) and ATT&CK techniques.

## What this tool does
Returns the name and description of a CWE, its type, the related CAPEC attack patterns, the ATT&CK techniques mapped
to those attack patterns, and the number of CVEs
linked to it, with how many of them are in the CISA KEV and EU KEV catalogs.

## When to use this tool
Use this tool when the user asks:
- "What is CWE-79?"
- "Which attack patterns are related to this weakness?"
- "Which ATT&CK techniques are related to this weakness?"
- "How often is this weakness exploited in the wild?"

## Inputs
- **cwe_id**: CWE identifier (`CWE-79` or `79`).

## Outputs
- `id`, `name`, `type`, `description`
- `capec`: related attack patterns, each with `id` and `name`
- `attack`: ATT&CK techniques mapped to these attack patterns (active techniques only), each with `id`, `name` and
  `via` (the CAPEC it comes from)
- `cve_count`: number of CVEs linked to this CWE
- `cisa_kev_count`: how many of these CVEs are in the CISA KEV catalog
- `eu_kev_count`: how many of these CVEs are in the EU KEV catalog
- `kev_count`: how many of these CVEs are in at least one of the two catalogs
- `url`: link to the CWE on SecDB

## LLM usage guidelines
- Do not explain a CWE from memory when the user needs the official definition: use this tool.
- Do not add `cisa_kev_count` and `eu_kev_count`: a CVE can be in both catalogs. Use `kev_count` for the total.
- Use `attack_info` for the details of an ATT&CK technique.
name: cwe_info

cisa_kev_count.description: Linked CVEs in the CISA KEV catalog

eu_kev_count.description: Linked CVEs in the EU KEV catalog

kev_count.description: Linked CVEs in at least one KEV catalog (CISA or EU)

url.description: Link to the CWE on SecDB
